correctness.rationale: Expansion of the exact energy-scaled Frobenius loss gives the strictly convex quadratic n/2-sum_i A_ii x_i+(1/2)sum_ij A_ij^2 x_i x_j. The Hessian A Hadamard A is SPD by Schur product; its normal equations reduce after correlation scaling to (R Hadamard R)w=1. Cramer determinants for a three-by-three SPD R yield d1x1=(1-t)(1+t-u-v)/Delta and cyclic analogues with u=a^2,v=b^2,t=c^2, Delta=1+2uvt-u^2-v^2-t^2>0. The sign inequalities and their equalities are necessary and sufficient, and two nonpositive coefficients would force one squared correlation >=1. Dimensions 1 and 2 always give positive coefficients. In the symmetric family R(r,s), 0<s<1 and 2r^2<1+s guarantee SPD; the optimum loses positivity exactly when (1+s^2)/2<r^2<(1+s)/2. A zero-first-coordinate KKT solution is the unique nonnegative optimum, with exact gap (2r^2-1-s^2)^2/[2(1+s^2)(1+s^2-2r^4)], while strictly positive fitting attains only its infimum. Independent rational checks recovered x=(-650,950,950)/889 and gap 4225/132461 for r=9/10,s=7/10, including leading principal minors.
